name: yeule
label: Ninja Tune
lede: yeule took a name from a Final Fantasy character at 14, hid behind it online from Singapore, and ended up with a Best New Music score for a fuzzy album about comforting their younger self.

eras.title: Hiding behind a game character
eras.text: yeule starts as a teenager's online persona in Singapore, stacks up EPs, and puts out a debut album while studying art in London. The sound is dream pop, made in a bedroom.

years.h: A Final Fantasy seeress lends yeule a name
years.p: Nat Ćmiel puts out a self-titled EP on March 3, 2014. The stage name comes from Paddra Nsu-Yeul, the reincarnating seeress of Final Fantasy XIII-2.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Ćmiel links the name to accepting mortality, and lists a jazz ensemble called Riot Diet before the solo project, with Final Fantasy and Kingdom Hearts soundtracks among the first sounds that stuck.

Ćmiel told The FADER they have used pseudonyms online since 14 and that the idea of personas felt freeing. Nat Ćmiel was just one of them: "it was on my fake ID too."

years.h: Three releases in ten months, ending with Coma
years.p: The Pathos EP lands on December 11, 2016, the Lost Memories Dot Net OST on July 17, 2017 and the Coma EP on September 27, 2017.
years.xp: Duncan Cooper of The FADER called Coma "dream-pop perfection", according to Wikipedia. Pathos was self-released and dedicated to David Singh.

years.p: The label will release the next two albums, Serotonin II and Glitch Princess.

years.h: Serotonin II arrives while yeule is still in art school
years.p: Tiny Mix Tapes gives the debut 4/5 and praises its sound design. yeule is at Central Saint Martins in London at the time.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Ćmiel applied to Central Saint Martins for fashion communication and womenswear, and graduated in 2020 with a Fine Arts degree. The debut was made in the middle of that.

eras.title: A face for the persona
eras.text: yeule adopts a cyber-gothic look, turns the pop up and brings in Danny L Harle and Mura Masa. Pitchfork notices.

years.cap: Yeule live at The Echo, Los Angeles
years.h: My Name Is Nat Ćmiel, a single under their own name
years.p: It drops at the end of 2020 and opens the campaign for Glitch Princess, the second album.

years.cap: Yeule at Pitchfork Music Festival, Chicago, July 16, 2022
years.h: A four-hour ambient track stretches Glitch Princess to 327 minutes
years.p: The digital edition tacks on "The Things They Did for Me Out of Love". Pitchfork gives the album 8.3 and Best New Music.
years.xp:
[[Danny L Harle|1fd94d42-5e6a-46f2-84bf-9cc0be6c009f]] produced five tracks, [[Mura Masa|d2a76e1b-cecc-4500-b445-d55591821cd3]] co-produced one, and the Japanese artist [[Tohji|8d76fa36-1f77-4105-b67e-02b596024dac]] appears on another. It came out on Bayonet with a Metacritic score of 85, according to Wikipedia; Clash and The Line of Best Fit each gave it 9/10.

yeule told The FADER they wanted to leave the "natural earthy Gothic Renaissance-esque world" for something "neo-technical, cyber-Gothic", with posthumanist ideas about AI and identity behind it.

q: The idea of personas have always been really freeing for me.
years.h: yeule says hello to the PC when they get home, goodnight when it's off
years.p: Interviewed by The FADER's Salvatore Maicki, yeule says personas have always felt freeing, and that treating devices nicely makes them nicer back.
years.xp:
The interview ran on February 4, 2022, the week Glitch Princess came out. The full line is that personas are freeing "because you don't get trapped in one body or one identity."

On their machines: "The more nice I treat my technological devices, the more I feel like they're nice to me too."

eras.title: Guitars up front, new label
eras.text: yeule signs to Ninja Tune and builds an album from old journal entries they call scars. The guitars move to the front and the reviews get better.

years.cap: Yeule during the softscars press cycle, c. 2023
years.h: sulky baby arrives with a Ninja Tune deal attached
years.p: On May 10, yeule announces the signing with their first new music since "Too Dead Inside", plus autumn shows in Chicago, New York, Los Angeles and London.
years.xp:
The dates: Metro in Chicago on October 10, Webster Hall in New York on October 15, The Fonda in Los Angeles on October 19, and Outernet in London on November 12.

DIY reported that the song grew out of old journals yeule calls scars, read aloud to generate material. yeule called it "a 2000s alt-rock shoegaze hybrid tinted in sad satire". The idea, in their words: "talking to a younger version of me, stopping her from crying."

years.h: dazies and fish in the pool go out together
years.p: Two more singles precede the album. Ghosts follows on August 9, Inferno on August 31 and the title track "softscars" on September 14.

years.cap: Yeule with their live band at End Of The Road, Larmer Tree Gardens, c. 2023
years.src: Wikipedia: Softscars · Album of the Year · Slant Magazine
years.h: Pitchfork scores Softscars 8.5, then ranks it No. 10 of 2023
years.p: Ryan Dombal's review makes it Best New Music. The third album is produced by yeule, [[Kin Leonn|11ed3790-f2a5-48fc-9a48-52c1f59cbab0]], [[Mura Masa|d2a76e1b-cecc-4500-b445-d55591821cd3]] and Chris Greatti, and Stereogum names it Album of the Week.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists a Metacritic score of 83, with The Line of Best Fit at 8/10 and PopMatters at 7/10.

Slant's Eric Mason wrote that yeule "expands, refines, and masters their creative vision". Physical copies followed on October 6.

eras.title: Heavier, and the critics split
eras.text: yeule leans further into 90s alt-rock and shoegaze. Pitchfork gives the fourth album 5.9; Clash gives it 9/10.

years.src: Wikipedia: Evangelic Girl Is a Gun
years.h: Eko comes out months before the album has a name
years.p: The single lands in late October 2024.

years.src: Wikipedia: Evangelic Girl Is a Gun · Wikipedia: Yeule
years.h: Skullcrusher brings in Clams Casino and Fitnesss
years.p: yeule announces the fourth album on March 3, the same day as the second single.
years.xp: [[Clams Casino|772a0eb3-fe31-4a08-b583-690296f44900]] and [[A.G. Cook|b12ef43e-72ad-43d0-b216-a8cd32f78852]] are among the producers on the album, along with Ćmiel, Fitnesss, Chris Greatti, Kin Leonn and Mura Masa, according to Wikipedia.

years.cap: Yeule at Great American Music Hall, San Francisco, September 23, 2025
years.src: Wikipedia: Evangelic Girl Is a Gun
yt: Evangelic Girl Is a Gun, official video
years.h: Pitchfork gives Evangelic Girl Is a Gun 5.9, Clash gives it 9/10
years.p: A 31-minute album that cites the painter Zdzislaw Beksinski. Metacritic lists 81 from ten critics.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the record as leaving the glitchy dream pop of Softscars for shoegaze, grunge and 90s alternative, with themes of self-destruction and literary romanticism. It reached No. 18 on the UK Independent Albums chart and No. 29 in Scotland.
